value.lineage: README: 'MAP-Elites module for Sferes2', reference 'Mouret, J. B., & Clune, J. (2015). Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites'; every licensed header says 'This file is a part of the sferes2 framework.' and the module builds via use='sferes2' with includes '../../' (i.e. lives at sferes2/modules/map_elites). sferes2's README at its own pin says 'we will soon integrate a more flexible version in the master branch of sferes_v2', i.e. this module is the standalone precursor of the later in-tree QD code. || main loop (reader, from the code): Per generation MapElites::epoch() flattens every occupied cell of the boost::multi_array archive into the working population, then Params::pop::size times picks two uniformly random elites, crosses and mutates them into two children, evaluates the whole child batch (in parallel via sferes::eval), and for each child computes its cell from round(desc_i * shape_i) and overwrites the occupant if the cell is empty, the child is fitter by more than epsilon, or it ties and lies closer to the cell centre; sferes2's Ea::run() drives this for nb_gen generations and dumps stats every dump_period.

organs.mechanism: p = min(1, descriptor), cell = round(p * n) clamped to n - 1
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: rounding against n makes cell 0 half-width and the last cell about 1.5 cells wide; negative descriptors are caught only by an assert

organs.mechanism: a living candidate enters an empty cell, or replaces the elite if better by more than epsilon, or if within epsilon and closer to the cell centre; the parent is stored beside it
organs.state: one elite and its parent per cell
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with epsilon > 0 a slightly worse but more central solution replaces the elite; the centre grid uses n - 1 while binning uses n (the test sets epsilon 0)

organs.mechanism: each generation rebuilds the population from occupied cells and, size times, draws two parents uniformly, crosses and mutates them and inserts both children with their parent
